task.title: Create and configure integrations
task.shortdesc: The Notifications administrator creates and configures integrations for the organization so third-party applications can send event notifications to users.

ul.li: You are logged into the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console as an Organization Administrator or as a user with Notifications administrator permissions.
Your endpoint must be protected by a non-self-signed and globally trusted certificate.

step.cmd: In the Hybrid Cloud Console, navigate to Settings > IntegrationsSettings > Integrations.
Select the tab for the type of integration you want to create. For example, to create a Slack integration, select the Communications tab.
Click Add integration and select the third-party tool to integrate with the Hybrid Cloud Console:

info.note: SSL is essential for protecting the data sent to the integration endpoint. SSL must always be used when integrating the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console with third-party applications.
SSL is essential for protecting the data sent to the integration endpoint.

substep.cmd: Optional: Provide a secret token, if required. If defined, the secret token is used as an X-Insight-Token header on the POST HTTP request.

info.note: A secret token is essential for protecting the data sent to the integration endpoint and should always be used when integrating the Hybrid Cloud Console with third-party applications.

step.cmd: To verify that the new integration is listed on the Integrations page, enter the integration name in Filter by Name box.

info.note: The new integration is enabled by default and available as an integration option when a Notifications administrator configures behavior groups in the notifications service. To disable the integration, toggle the switch in the Enabled column. To configure a behavior group, see .
